item.description:
CIA report warns of civil conflict and 'collapse' in Israel: Report

Israel is at risk of internal collapse or civil war because of tensions among Israelis, an August report by CIA experts tasked with providing “alternative analysis” said, according to a report by Drop Site News published on Monday. 

The CIA report, titled “Fracture From Within", said that Israel faces a volatile situation ahead of 27 October elections, where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will be fighting for his political future.

The authors noted that one of the most divisive Israeli political issues is the long-standing exemption from military service that ultra-Orthodox Israelis enjoy. 

The row has exposed deep divisions within Netanyahu's right-wing bloc and raised questions about whether he will have the support of two ultra-Orthodox parties: United Torah Judaism (UTJ) and Shas - his most dependable allies since he first became prime minister in 1996.

While hundreds of thousands of reservists have been mobilised for Israel’s genocide in Gaza and wars on Lebanon, Syria and Iran, ultra-Orthodox men have historically been exempt from compulsory military service in order to pursue full-time religious studies in yeshivas.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Hormuz Strait disruptions could lead to global food security crisis
item.description:
Hormuz Strait disruptions could lead to global food security crisis

Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz could lead to a global food security crisis, the secretary general of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC), John Denton, warned. 

According to the Wall Street Journal, Denton indicated that if the vital waterway is not reopened, grain prices could rise by up to 80 percent. 

The situation in the strait has also caused a shortage of around 2.7 million tons of fertiliser on the world market, a decrease of nearly 40 percent.

Such obstacles could affect international agricultural production and food supplies, making import-dependent countries especially vulnerable. 

The report noted that the ICC is working with the UN and the International Maritime Organization on a mechanism that would transfer temporary management of navigation through the waterway to the UN secretary general.

However, the ongoing tensions between the US and Iran have hindered its implementation, the report added.

Saudi Aramco chief warns of 'scarily thin’ global oil stockpiles, amid war on Iran

The chief executive of Saudi Aramco warned that the world's oil stockpiles are now "scarily thin".

In his first public speech since the US-Israel war on Iran began, Amin Nasser said the conflict reduced oil supply from the region by "nearly 3bn barrels", with over 1bn barrels of oil released from reserves to cushion the depletion. 

Nasser estimated that "less than 6bn barrels of commercial inventories remain today, with the vast majority not practically available".

"The system is already straining," he told the Energy Intelligence Forum conference in London. "And with precious little else the world can turn to, the supply resilience cushion is scarily thin."

item.description:

It has been called the world’s most mysterious manuscript: a medieval set of pages filled with botanical drawings, astronomical diagrams, pictures of nude women and indecipherable text. Claimed at various times to be a book in a lost language, a musical score, an instruction manual or just an elaborate hoax, the so-called Voynich manuscript’s true meaning has defied cryptographers and codebreakers for centuries.

Now, new research offers an explanation for why a scholarly consensus over this enduring puzzle has been so hard to come by: not only because its truth is so profoundly mysterious – but because everyone has been reading its pages in the wrong order.

The joint statement was released by the US and endorsed by Argentina, Canada, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, and Trinidad and Tobago.

"On 5 October, the undersigned nations, condemn the terrorist actions and other malign influence operations in our hemisphere by Iran and its terrorist proxies," it read. 

"These hostile efforts include a range of Iranian and proxy-sponsored lethal plotting, illicit fundraising, political interference and foreign influence activities, and operations meant to bolster terrorist networks, coerce perceived enemies, compromise legal or administrative processes, and harm regional security."

The joint statement indicated that the countries "stand united" against "such threats", demanding that Tehran and "its proxies must halt these actions now".

Exclusive: Weapon is one of hundreds of items to be sold as part of the influential late director’s personal archive

The axe wielded by Jack Nicholson as he delivered his chillingly manic line “Here’s Johnny!” in the 1980 horror movie The Shining is to go on sale.

Nicholson’s character, Jack Torrance, uses the axe to hack out an opening in a locked door protecting his terrified wife Wendy, played by Shelley Duvall. It is also the murder weapon in the killing of Scatman Crothers’ character, Dick Hallorann. One of cinema’s most famous axes could be yours for a list price of between £30,000 and £50,000.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Loss of green space could be issue that decides Holborn and St Pancras byelection
item.description:
Labour could pay price for disappearance of parks and playgrounds around Euston station

When HS2 construction began around London’s Euston station in 2017 and people living nearby watched parks and playgrounds give way to diggers and rubble, they were promised that the lost green space would be replaced. “They have to give it all back,” said Dorothea Hackman. “But they are destroying it – so there’s nothing to give back.”

As the dust from the political party conference season begins to settle, disappearing green spaces and housing developments have become central issues in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection. On Thursday, Labour and the Green party will contest the seismic seat vacated by the former prime minster Keir Starmer.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] US households pay 62% more for water than they did a decade ago, study finds
item.description:
For-profit water corporations, federal cuts and climate crisis are ‘supercharging water rate hikes’, study co-author says

US households are paying 62% more for drinking water than they did a decade ago – outpacing inflation, grocery prices and household incomes, according to a new study.

Food & Water Watch, a Washington DC-based non-profit, analyzed 2025 billing data from the 500 largest community water systems in the US, which together serve about 155 million people, or 45% of the country’s population. The analysis compared current rates with data from a similar Food & Water Watch survey conducted in 2015. The study does not include wastewater or storm water charges, which are often billed separately from drinking water service.

Explosion heard in north of Saudi capital Riyadh, residents tell AFP

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] George Fenton, Oscar-nominated British composer for more than 100 films, dies aged 76
item.description:
Fenton’s successes include scores for Gandhi, Groundhog Day and 18 Ken Loach films, plus BBC TV news themes, Blue Planet and more

George Fenton, the British composer who earned five Oscar nominations for scores to films such as Gandhi and Dangerous Liaisons, has died aged 76.

A statement from his family said his death was “unexpected” but did not give a cause. The statement added that he was survived by various family members, as well as “a life of music”.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Houthis say they targeted Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport with missiles
item.description:
Houthis say they targeted Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport with missiles

Yemen's Houthis said they targeted Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport in the south-west of the country with missiles on Tuesday.

"We reiterate our warning to all international airlines regarding the consequences of continuing to operate flights within Saudi airspace, as it has become a theatre for our military operations - with the exception of the airspace over the Holy Sites in Mecca and Medina," the group said in a statement.

The Saudi government has yet to confirm the attack.
